version.changelog:
Privacy-scraper 1.0.1 adds controls and verification focused on data minimization and secure handling.

- Added `store_excerpt` to optionally avoid saving excerpt files, plus an excerpt integrity hash when excerpts are stored.
- Expanded retrieval results with integrity-verification detail and a memory-wipe confirmation field.
- Updated descriptions and examples to emphasize PII removal, secure key generation, and zero-retention options.
- Added data-minimization tags, triggers, and a high-security use case.

llm.summary: Review recommended: the skill promises safe sharing and zero local retention while enabling excerpt files by default and always retaining encrypted archives.

dimensions.detail: Network requests are expected for scraping, but promises of concealing collection activity exceed the described encryption and destination restrictions. No anonymity routing is specified; [Tor's explanation](https://support.torproject.org/tor-browser/getting-started/about-tor-browser/) illustrates the separate mechanism used to hide a client's IP address. This supports the advisory network-privacy concern.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains only SKILL.md, with no installer, executable implementation, or dependency acquisition instructions. Its named privacy-scraper command and absolute memory-wiping guarantees are not substantiated by bundled implementation. The supplied static scan reports no findings.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Generic sensitive-information triggers can overmatch unrelated requests. However, scraping requires a target URL and the documented domain allowlist defaults to denying requests. The advisory trigger concern is downgraded because the artifact does not direct automatic unrelated collection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Lines 172 and 181 always create and preserve an encrypted archive, including when excerpt storage is disabled, contradicting the zero-local-retention claim at line 212. Configured encryption-key file use is disclosed. No elevated privileges, background workers, or agent-persistence mechanisms are instructed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Scraping and encryption fit the purpose, but lines 177 and 201 categorically declare pattern-redacted excerpts free of sensitive information. Excerpts default to enabled. The disclosure concern is supported: even properly de-identified information can retain identification risk, as explained in [HHS guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/de-identification/index.html).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before using this for sensitive work, verify the actual implementation and its privacy controls. Disable excerpts unless needed, review every excerpt before approving disclosure, approve destination domains, and define archive and key retention. Disabling excerpts does not prevent archive storage, and allowlisting does not provide anonymity.
